title: AppClient
description:
A client of the app: a web app, a SPA, a native app, a CLI or a service. Its
`grant_types` and redirect URIs are its OAuth config, and OpenID Connect is
OAuth plus the `openid` scope, so one shape serves both. A confidential client
without `grant_types` holds only credentials, and turns on client credentials
later without becoming a new principal.

slug.description: Stable identifier of the client, unique among the app's clients and APIs. Other documents and the console name it as `<app>/<client>`.

name.description: Shown on the consent screen in place of the app's name. Optional.

client_id.description:
The `client_id` the client presents. Leave it out and the server mints one the first time
the client is written. Set it to keep an id a client already has: one compiled into a desktop
or mobile app, one a v4 or another identity provider issued, or one every project the release
ships to should share. Either way it is fixed for the life of the client: a revision that
changes it is refused, and a revision that leaves it out keeps it. Unique within the project,
and never in a form the server mints (`client_` or `dcr_` followed by an id).

type.description: `public` clients (SPAs, native apps, CLIs) hold no credential and prove themselves with PKCE alone, so they only act for the user who signed in. `confidential` clients hold credentials and authenticate with any of them: a secret (`client_secret_basic` or `client_secret_post`) or a key (`private_key_jwt`).

secret.description:
A secret of a client declared in the release, as a `${{ NAME }}` reference to a project
variable (ADR 062), never the value itself. The server reads the variable from the deployment
when the client authenticates. Optional: a confidential client can hold secrets and keys
written through the API instead, or beside it, which a deploy never removes. An app
registered through the API holds no reference.

jwks.description: Public keys the confidential client signs its `private_key_jwt` assertions with, as a JWK set. Public members only, so a private key can never be committed. Keys written through the API count too.

grant_types.description:
The grant types the client may use, with RFC 7591's name and values. `authorization_code`
signs a user in with PKCE (every client, OAuth 2.1); `refresh_token` keeps a grant alive;
`client_credentials` lets a confidential client act as itself, so the tokens it gets have the
client as `sub`. A public client needs `authorization_code` and may not use
`client_credentials`. A confidential client that leaves it out holds only credentials, and
then takes none of the fields below.

redirect_uris.description:
Where the authorization endpoint may send the user back, matched exactly. A loopback
`http://127.0.0.1`, `http://[::1]` or `http://localhost` URI matches on any port (RFC 8252
§7.3), and a public client may use a private-use scheme such as `com.example.app:/callback`
(RFC 8252 §7.1). Required with `authorization_code`, and only with it.

post_logout_redirect_uris.description: Where RP-initiated logout may send the user afterwards, matched exactly.

first_party.description: A first-party client skips consent unless the request asks for it (ADR 082 §3). When left out, a client of an app declared in the release is first-party and a client of an app registered through the API is not.

consent.description:
When the user is asked to consent. `skip` never asks unless the request says `prompt=consent`,
and only a first-party client may skip. `new_scopes` asks for scopes the user has not consented
to yet. `always` asks on every request. Defaults to `skip` for a first-party client and
`new_scopes` for a third-party one.

account_choice.description: Lets the user pick an account, or sign in as someone else, when a session is already live (ADR 081 §11). A request asks for it with `prompt=select_account` either way.

id_token_signed_response_alg.description: The algorithm the client's ID tokens are signed with. RS256 when left out (ADR 082 §7).

apis.description:
The APIs the client may get access tokens for, its default first. A token is for one API
(RFC 8707): the request names it with `resource`, and a request for an API not listed here
fails with `invalid_target`.

AppClientJwk.title: AppClientJWK
AppClientJwk.description: One public key (RFC 7517). Private members (`d`, `p`, `q`, `k` and the rest) are not accepted.

api.description: An API of this app by its slug, or an API of another app in the project as `<app>/<api>`.

scopes.description: The API's scopes the client may get. Leave it out for every scope the API defines. A request for any other scope fails with `invalid_scope`.
